_syllabus_items.title: Technology: the impact of e-commerce and digital communication on business
Ethical and environmental considerations: ethical trade-offs, environmental impacts (congestion, recycling, waste, pollution) and sustainability
The economic climate on businesses: interest rates, the level of employment and consumer spending
Globalisation: how UK businesses compete internationally (design, quality, pricing) and the effect of exchange rates
Legislation: employment law, health and safety law, and consumer law
Competitive environment: the impact of operating in competitive markets, and the uncertainty and risks businesses face
Production processes: job and flow production, lean production and just in time (JIT)
The role of procurement: JIT and just in case (JIC) stock management, supplier selection, and supply-chain management
The concept of quality: consequences of poor quality, total quality management (TQM), and the costs and benefits of quality
Good customer service: product knowledge, after-sales service, customer satisfaction/loyalty, reputation risk, and the impact of ICT
Organisational structures: span of control, chain of command, delayering and delegation, tall vs. flat structures and their effect on communication
Recruitment and selection: internal and external recruitment, job analysis/description/person specification, selection methods, and full-time/part-time/job-share/zero-hours contracts
Motivating employees: financial methods (salary, wage, commission, profit sharing) and non-financial methods (management style, training, responsibility, fringe benefits)
Training: induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training, and their effect on productivity, quality, technology adoption and retention
Identifying and understanding customers: why businesses need to know their customers (product fit, sales, marketing mix, avoiding costly mistakes, competitiveness)
Segmentation: dividing a market by gender, age, location and income

The purpose and methods of market research: primary research (questionnaires, surveys, interviews, focus groups) and secondary research (internet, printed press), qualitative vs. quantitative data, market size and market share

The marketing mix (4Ps): price (skimming, penetration, competitive, loss leader, cost-plus), product (USP, brand image, product life cycle, extension strategies, product portfolio), promotion (advertising, PR, sales promotion, sponsorship, social media) and place (retailers, wholesalers, telesales, e-commerce/m-commerce)

Sources of finance: internal (retained profit, sale of assets) and external (family/friends, share issue, loans/mortgages, overdraft, trade credit, hire purchase, government grants), and their suitability
Cash flow: why cash matters, the consequences of cash-flow problems, how and why cash-flow forecasts are built, net cash flow and opening/closing balances, and solutions to cash-flow problems
Financial terms and calculations: fixed/variable/total costs, revenue, costs, profit and loss, break-even output and margin of safety (read from a chart), and average rate of return
Analysing the financial performance of a business: the income statement and statement of financial position, assets vs. liabilities, and gross/net profit margin
